newsitem.title: USA: Strength in big name tech stocks boosts Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: Strength in big name tech stocks boosts Nasdaq.

text.p: A boost in several large technology companies propelled Nasdaq shares higher Tuesday for the fourth consecutive session, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index gained strength throughout the day, ending up about six points or 0.48 percent to an unofficial close of 1257.37. The Dow industrials closed up 53 points to 6609.
"The worst could be over for the techs. The gains over the past few days don't make up for the weakness, but it certainly is good to get back on track," one trader said.

Dell Computer Corp surged five to to 78-3/4 after J.P. Morgan initiated coverage of the personal computer maker as a buy. Microsoft Corp added 2-3/8 to 98-1/4 and Intel Corp firmed 1-31/64 to 146-39/64.

Less fortunate was Viking Office Products Inc, which fell 5-1/2 to 14-1/2 after the company forecast third quarter earnings below Wall Street expectations. Alex. Brown also downgraded the stock to buy from strong buy.
Overall, advancing issues and declining issues were almost equal, with 2080 gainers and 2089 losers, on total volume of 531 million shares. Fifty-eight issues hit new highs and 167 hit new lows.
